content.title: About
content.content: Flavored rice, brown and wild is a blend of whole‑grain brown rice and wild rice grains seasoned with natural herbs and spices. It offers a rich nutty flavor, subtle aromatic notes, and a firm texture while retaining the nutritional benefits of whole grains.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The combination of brown and wild rice provides a more complex flavor and texture than plain white rice.
Wild rice is not a true rice but the seed of several aquatic grasses native to North America.
Brown rice retains the bran and germ, making it more nutritious than polished white rice.
Seasonings typically include dried garlic, onion, paprika, and herbs such as thyme or rosemary, without artificial additives.
The blend is popular in low‑glycemic diets because of its slower impact on blood sugar.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Both brown and wild rice supply dietary fiber that supports healthy digestion.

items.title: Source of magnesium and selenium
items.content: These minerals aid muscle function, nerve health, and antioxidant protection.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: Helps maintain stable blood glucose levels, beneficial for pre‑diabetic individuals.

items.title: Contains plant protein
items.content: Provides about 7 g of protein per 100 g, contributing to satiety.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Phytonutrients in brown and wild rice help combat free radicals.

items.title: Rice allergy
items.content: A small number of people may experience allergic reactions to rice.

items.title: Arsenic content
items.content: Brown rice can accumulate trace amounts of arsenic; varied grain consumption is advised.

items.title: Digestive sensitivity
items.content: High fiber may cause gas or bloating in sensitive individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Flavored rice, brown and wild can be cooked as a side dish, added to salads, soups, bowls, or casseroles. Rinse the rice, then simmer 1 part rice to 2 parts water for 20‑25 minutes until tender but still slightly firm.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. For storage longer than six months, keep in the refrigerator to prevent mold growth.
